title: Contracts between Firms and Stakeholders

scopes.description: Full author-supplied workflow: download SC 13D filings for the 1996–2018 Stata sample in Python, parse filings in Perl, manually import the pipe-delimited handoff in SAS Enterprise, merge SEC Analytics/Compustat-CRSP/CRSP/TFN/I-B/E/S inputs in SAS, export the master Stata file, and run the supplied Stata tables. The program sources are embedded in PDFs and there is no supported separate analysis-only route.

requirements.description: Raw EDGAR filing text for the supplied SAS target form SC 13D over the Stata sample period 1996–2018. The SAS branch deletes every SEC Analytics row whose form is not exactly SC 13D, so SC 13D/A amendments are outside this supplied target. The Perl parser consumes filing documents and writes the intermediate results table.

routes.description: Official public source route for the requested filing type and period; EDGAR indexes begin in 1994Q3. Configure the downloaded documents as Perl input. Respect request limits and set an identifying User-Agent.
routes.expected_period: SC 13D filings in 1996–2018; actual document coverage and filename mapping remain to be validated.

routes.description: Both approved local roots exist, but no listing, format, form coverage, date coverage or compatibility check was performed. Candidate only.

requirements.description: Author-named homed.SEC_Analytics_Jordan table. The SAS source reads CIK, FORM, SECFNAME and FDATE to filter SC 13D, build a filename suffix, and establish the filing year; additional columns are carried downstream and need a full schema/lineage contract. Its filename2 key must match the Perl output filename2 transformation.

routes.description: Catalog candidate has CIK, FORM, SECFNAME and FDATE but its product, population, history, extra fields, row coverage and compatibility with SEC_Analytics_Jordan are unverified. Do not assume raw SEC filings or this candidate supply the author linkage product.
routes.expected_period: SC 13D filing records matching the 1996–2018 sample; history and completeness unknown.

requirements.description: Author-named homed.compcrsp_merged_jan2019 input. SAS derives YEAR from DATADATE and joins by CIK/YEAR; downstream code also uses GVKEY, LPERMNO, SIC, CUSIP and Compustat controls. The supplied package does not include its producer or the crosswalk/transformation contract.

routes.description: One-row probe verifies raw annual fundamentals columns, but this is not the author-prepared Compustat/CRSP merged input and does not establish CIK-year matching, LPERMNO/SIC linkage, source selection or required period coverage.
routes.expected_period: Records matching 1996–2018 filing CIK/year; exact construction/history is unspecified.

requirements.description: CRSP Daily Stock File fields PERMNO, DATE, RET, ASK, BID, PRC, SHROUT and VOL. The supplied SAS calculates the event window [−5,+5] weekdays and a pre-event window from 365 calendar days before the filing date up to but excluding five weekdays before it; Stata then samples filing years 1996–2018.

routes.description: Exact catalog-listed CRSP daily stock product is locally readable in a bounded one-row probe with all source-read fields. The current source uses the WRDS remote CRSP.DSF libref; using this local candidate requires configuring an equivalent local read while preserving the supplied SQL, and full coverage remains unverified.
routes.expected_period: For each 1996–2018 filing date: at least 365 calendar days before through five weekdays after; verify population/history.

requirements.description: CRSP daily index fields DATE, VWRETD and EWRETD, joined to filing dates for cumulative market benchmark returns over [−5,+5] weekdays.

routes.description: Exact catalog-listed daily index table is locally readable in a bounded one-row probe with all source-read fields. The current code queries it inside a WRDS remote session; local execution requires a compatible local placement of the supplied query. Full coverage is unverified.
routes.expected_period: For each 1996–2018 filing date, at least five weekdays before through five weekdays after; verify history.

requirements.description: Thomson-Reuters 13F holdings table TFN.S34 with CUSIP, RDATE, SHARES and SHROUT1. SAS filters report dates before 1993, removes missing values, derives CUSIP6 and year-quarter, and joins holdings to filings by CUSIP6/year-quarter.

routes.description: The exact product/schema is catalogued, but the bounded local read timed out; this does not establish absence or licensing. Verify actual readability and required period coverage before using it.
routes.expected_period: 1993 onward through filing quarters in 1996–2018; verify available coverage.

requirements.description: Author-prepared I/B/E/S input ibes.eps_consensus_unadjusted_1994 with DATE, PERMNO and NUM_FORECAST. SAS keeps dates from 1993 onward, forms year-quarter, averages NUM_FORECAST by PERMNO/quarter and joins to the filing quarter.

routes.description: The local unadjusted US EPS summary candidate is readable with TICKER, STATPERS, MEASURE, FPI and NUMEST, but it does not demonstrate the author-prepared PERMNO/DATE/NUM_FORECAST contract or a supported identifier mapping. It is not the same variable family as a GPS substitution.
routes.expected_period: Candidate observations start in an unverified history; the author input is filtered to 1993 onward.

requirements.description: CRSP stock-name effective history with PERMNO, ST_DATE and END_DATE. SAS sorts history, retains the first PERMNO start date, and joins an interval active on FILEDATE to derive company age.

routes.description: Exact catalog-listed table is locally readable in a bounded one-row probe with all source-read fields. The complete effective-date history and coverage for the 1996–2018 sample remain to be checked.
routes.expected_period: Must include first available PERMNO date and effective-name intervals for the filing sample in 1996–2018.

issues.description: The full target crosses PDF-embedded Python helpers, Perl, a manual SAS Enterprise import, SAS data libraries/export and Stata. Author paths are Windows/Dropbox-specific. The handoff must preserve the Perl pipe schema, rawd.results, all SAS inputs and the master.dta producer/consumer order.

The active downloader sets PARM_FORMS to 10-K and PARM_BGNYEAR/PARM_ENDYEAR to 2018/1996; its ascending range is empty. The downstream SAS selector and Stata sample support configuring the working copy for SC 13D and inclusive years 1996–2018.

The Python program calls time.clock(), which is absent in the available Python 3.12 runtime; the companion helper also calls misspelled time.strfime() in its retry-error path. These are working-copy compatibility fixes, not a need to alter the PDFs.
HTML::Strip is imported by the Perl parser but was not found in the checked environment; File::Find and List::MoreUtils are available.

SAS startup failed at TKELS, and availability of SAS/CONNECT, the SAS PC Files interface for DBMS=STATA and the author-described SAS Enterprise manual import interface is unverified. These findings do not establish a missing license.

SEC_Analytics_Jordan is an exact author-named SAS input whose full field list, product lineage, filename convention, history/coverage and relation to local WRDSSEC candidates are unspecified. Raw filings and SEC_ITEM_SCORES are not proven substitutes.

The supplied SAS source consumes compcrsp_merged_jan2019 but does not provide its producer or complete CIK/year/GVKEY/PERMNO/SIC/CUSIP field, linking and coverage contract. COMP.FUNDA is a raw annual candidate, not a demonstrated replacement.
TFN.S34 has a catalog-listed matching schema, but the exact bounded read timed out; local availability and coverage from 1993 through the filing quarters remain unverified.

The author expects eps_consensus_unadjusted_1994 with DATE, PERMNO and NUM_FORECAST. The local unadjusted EPS summary candidate instead exposes TICKER, STATPERS and NUMEST; no mapping or equivalence is supplied.

The Stata program uses flesch_reading_ease and ind_corporate, and its industry regressions use ind_code1 through ind_code12. No producer for these fields is present in the supplied Perl/SAS code; SAS creates only scalar ind_code. A prepared input may supply them, but that contract is unknown.
The Stata source says Table 6 is created manually but provides no recipe, input contract or validation checks. The supplied code alone cannot close the full documented table target.

Programs are embedded in PDFs rather than supplied as standalone runnable files. Extract working copies from all Python, Perl, SAS and Stata program PDFs and verify page-wrap-sensitive statements before any separately authorized run.

evidence.description: SAS librefs use a Windows project directory; the program expects manual SAS Enterprise import of Perl results.txt as rawd.results.
SAS filters SEC_Analytics_Jordan to form exactly SC 13D and links to Perl output through a normalized filename suffix.
SAS expects compcrsp_merged_jan2019, creates year from DATADATE and joins on CIK/year.
Remote CRSP.DSF query calculates firm measures in the filing-date weekday window from −5 to +5.

163       create table for_crsp_firm_annc_pm5 as
164       select a.id,
165           EXP(sum(log(1+b.RET)))-1 as firmreturns_pm5,

evidence.description: Exact Stata eststo command check succeeded in Stata 18 using the frozen software helper.

actions.description: Extract the embedded programs to working copies and configure a single relative execution root that preserves every producer and consumer directory. Do not edit the source PDFs.
steps: Use a runtime working directory of ./replication_work and create code/python, code/perl, code/sas, code/stata, data/edgar, logs, intermediate/perl, sasdata/rawd, sasdata/homed, sasdata/ibes, sasdata/crspsk, stata and stata/tables beneath it.

Extract the _1_ Python driver and all three helpers into code/python together; extract the Perl, SAS and Stata programs from their PDF containers to their respective code directories, checking page wraps and statement boundaries.
Point PARM_PATH and the Perl recursive input root at data/edgar; put Perl filelist.txt and results.txt under intermediate/perl. Preserve the parser header and pipe delimiter.

Import intermediate/perl/results.txt manually in SAS Enterprise as rawd.results under sasdata/rawd. Set homed, ibes and crspsk to the corresponding sasdata subdirectories while preserving the exact SEC_Analytics_Jordan, compcrsp_merged_jan2019, EPS and stocknames table names.

Set SAS PROC EXPORT output to stata/master.dta; set the Stata use path to the same file and its table-output global to stata/tables. Keep the source remote CRSP/TFN branch and all other merge steps until a compatible input route is verified.
validation: Before any separately authorized run, verify each configured directory is visible and writable from the SAS and Stata batch processes.
After Perl output is produced, compare the pipe header and record structure with the manual SAS import variables; verify rawd.results is the imported producer table.
After SAS export, verify master.dta exists at the Stata consumer path and contains all expected upstream columns before running Stata.

actions.description: Configure the extracted downloader for the exact form and sample that the supplied SAS and Stata branch retains. Set the start year before the end year because the author loop is ascending and inclusive.
steps: In the extracted working copy, set PARM_FORMS to the exact EDGAR form string SC 13D, PARM_BGNYEAR to 1996 and PARM_ENDYEAR to 2018; retain the inclusive end-year loop and do not select SC 13D/A, which the downstream SAS filter deletes.
Keep the four-quarter annual loop and point its form/year output under data/edgar. Do not rely on the inactive EDGAR_Forms.f_13D alternative.
Configure an identifying User-Agent for SEC requests and keep request pacing within the SEC published maximum rate.
validation: Review generated master-index selections for form SC 13D and years 1996–2018 before filing downloads.
Compare downloaded filing names with the suffix normalization used to build filename2 in SAS; verify SC 13D/A is not included in the retained SAS sample.

actions.description: Make the Python code compatible with the verified runtime by repairing only timing and logging API calls in extracted working copies.
steps: In extracted _1_EDGAR_DownloadForms and _1_EDGAR_Pac working copies, replace each elapsed-duration use of time.clock() with time.perf_counter(); keep the surrounding timing logic intact.
In the _1_EDGAR_Pac exception handler, correct the misspelled time.strfime() call to time.strftime() so the retry path can log errors.
Leave the PDF originals unchanged and preserve the download/filter logic.
validation: Use a self-written Python 3.12 syntax and API check on extracted helper copies; confirm timing and error-log function names resolve without importing author modules.
After a later authorized run, exercise normal logging and a controlled non-network exception path; do not download files during preparation.

actions.description: Provide the HTML::Strip module required by the Perl parser in the selected Perl 5.40.1 environment.
steps: Install HTML::Strip through the approved Perl environment/package channel, or configure PERL5LIB to an already-approved compatible module location. Do not replace the parser HTML stripping behavior.
Keep the verified File::Find and List::MoreUtils dependencies in the same Perl environment.
validation: Run an isolated Perl module require/version check for HTML::Strip and the two existing modules; do not execute the author parser.

actions.description: Establish the SAS runtime and each component used by the manual import, remote merge and Stata export stages. Current probes are unverified, not evidence of an absent license.
steps: Resolve the observed TKELS startup failure or otherwise verify the installed SAS 9.4 batch runtime with the Base SAS procedures in the supplied source.
Confirm SAS/CONNECT availability and WRDS access for SIGNON, RSUBMIT, UPLOAD and DOWNLOAD, including the expected interactive credential handoff.
Confirm the licensed SAS PC Files Interface supports DBMS=STATA export and that the author-described SAS Enterprise manual import interface is available for the pipe-delimited results.txt handoff.
validation: Before running author code, verify SAS startup in the intended batch environment and confirm each required component through product documentation or local entitlement records.
Use a small authorized-format check only after the runtime is established; do not execute the author merge or export during this assessment.

actions.description: Acquire only the public filing text needed for the configured SC 13D, 1996–2018 branch and place it in the configured Perl input tree.
steps: Use SEC EDGAR full-index records for SC 13D in 1996–2018 and retrieve the corresponding filing text; preserve the SEC accession/file suffix used by the Perl-to-SAS filename2 link.
Use a descriptive User-Agent and comply with the published request limit. The existing local SEC roots may be checked later for coverage, but directory existence alone is not a filing corpus.
validation: Check form and year bounds against index metadata and verify document readability and filename compatibility before Perl parsing.
Confirm the downstream SAS exact-form filter retains the intended records and report linkage coverage; do not broaden to amendments without a separate supplied target.

Confirm how SECFNAME and the Perl filename are normalized to filename2 and which records are in scope under the exact SC 13D filter.

Treat WRDSSEC.SEC_ITEM_SCORES as a catalog candidate only; shared metadata columns do not establish equal population, additional fields or equivalence. Raw SEC filings do not supply this linkage table by themselves.

validation: With authorized inputs, compare requested columns and types and verify coverage/history for the analysis sample; do not treat one-row probe ranges as full-history evidence.

If using IBES.STATSUMU_EPSUS as a candidate, obtain documented identifier mapping and variable derivation for TICKER, STATPERS and NUMEST to the author DATE, PERMNO and NUM_FORECAST contract; do not guess NUMEST is an alias or substitute a GPS series.

steps: Confirm whether the intended master input supplies flesch_reading_ease, ind_corporate and ind_code1 through ind_code12, and provide their documented producer, definitions and source columns.
The supplied SAS creates scalar ind_code and the supplied Stata source creates corporate; do not infer that either is equivalent to the missing fields or manufacture indicators.

actions.description: Obtain the author manual Table 6 procedure and required inputs to close the full documented table target.
steps: Request the manual Table 6 recipe, source fields and inputs, transformations, table layout and verification checks.
Do not infer the table construction from the paper or substitute a new analysis.
validation: Compare the provided recipe and input contract with the supplied master data and confirm Table 6 checks before claiming full table coverage.

actions.description: After the required inputs, code working copies, paths and software are prepared, run the author workflow in its actual cross-language order.
steps: From ./replication_work, run the extracted Python downloader and produce the configured SEC filing tree.
Run the extracted Perl parser against that tree and produce intermediate/perl/results.txt.
Manually import results.txt in SAS Enterprise as rawd.results, then run the supplied SAS merges, including the WRDS branch and all source inputs, and export stata/master.dta.
Run the extracted Stata program against stata/master.dta and save supplied tables under stata/tables. Complete Table 6 only after its manual recipe is supplied.
validation: At each handoff, verify producer file, schema, key variables, expected period and consumer path before advancing.
Record software versions, manual import settings, record/linkage counts and unresolved rows; execution remains unverified until performed under separate authorization.

review_notes: The frozen dependency checklist is empty and the static audit reports no supported code. The actual PDF-embedded programs were traced directly; code-derived inputs and handoffs are recorded here rather than treating parser silence as closure.
The 26,486-line identifiers PDF is a filing-ID/date list only. It is not a prepared analysis dataset and does not justify an analysis_only scope.
FactSet is named in documentation but no supplied SAS input read for FactSet was found. Audit Analytics appears only as a Stata cross-check comment; neither is added as a live input requirement.
The SAS local-data probes are one-row readability/field checks only. They do not establish historical coverage or author-specific prepared dataset equivalence.
Source references use the work item cached text line ranges; program code is embedded in PDF containers and is not directly executable.

The existing local CRSP one-row probes verify table readability and required columns, not full event/history coverage. Their locations can support a local route only after configuring the supplied queries appropriately; current code places the source queries inside SAS/CONNECT RSUBMIT.

The SEC filing target follows the explicit SAS SC 13D selector. The companion 13-D constant is inactive, and the SAS branch excludes SC 13D/A by exact form matching; no amendment-scope clarification is required for this supplied branch.

The SEC form/year configuration is a routine working-copy choice supported by the downstream exact SC 13D filter and inclusive 1996–2018 sample. The code current 2018-to-1996 ascending range is empty; no descending-loop rewrite is proposed.
Actions that mention code changes apply only to extracted working copies; no PDF or author code was modified or executed. No data were downloaded and no packages were installed.

The complete source closure is not established because SEC_Analytics_Jordan and compcrsp_merged_jan2019 have no supplied producers/contracts, TFN and I/B/E/S routes remain unresolved, Stata has unproduced field references, and Table 6 is manual.
SAS/STAT is not listed as a separate dependency because the source uses PROC UNIVARIATE, which the frozen rules attribute to Base SAS.
Exact Stata software checks cover winsor, eststo, estpost, estadd, esttab, reghdfe and ftools; all are separated by the command keys used in the probes.
